\chapter{Third-Party Provider Integration Tests} \label{cap:thirdparty}

Provider integration tests are located in \texttt{src/test/java/com/example/meetings/discover/ProviderIntegrationTest.java}.

These tests use \texttt{MockRestServiceServer} to verify the integration contract without depending on live Ticketmaster, SeatGeek, or AgendaLx services. This choice avoids network flakiness, API credentials, rate limits, and changing third-party data. The providers still execute their real mapping and error-handling code; only the remote HTTP endpoint is simulated.

Covered behavior includes:

\begin{itemize}
\item Ticketmaster response mapping.
\item Ticketmaster unconfigured state.
\item Ticketmaster malformed event filtering.
\item Ticketmaster HTTP error handling.
\item Ticketmaster query parameter encoding.
\item SeatGeek response mapping.
\item SeatGeek fallback from \texttt{title} to \texttt{short\_title}.
\item SeatGeek malformed event filtering.
\item SeatGeek HTTP error handling.
\item AgendaLx response mapping.
\item AgendaLx user-agent usage.
\item AgendaLx past occurrence filtering.
\item AgendaLx blank title filtering.
\item AgendaLx fallback to 20:00 Europe/Lisbon when no time is parseable.
\item AgendaLx HTTP error handling.
\end{itemize}

The Ticketmaster query-encoding test intentionally fails. It asserts that query parameters such as spaces should be encoded exactly once, but the current provider produces \texttt{\%2520}, showing that an already-encoded value is encoded a second time.

The discovery-level provider aggregation behavior is tested separately in \texttt{DiscoveryServiceTest}. That test verifies that an outage in one configured provider should not prevent results from other providers. It currently errors because \texttt{DiscoveryService} does not catch provider exceptions.
